'''Corperryale Lādorable''' "'''Manny'''" '''Harris''' (born September 21, 1989) is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who last played for [[Al Riyadi Beirut]] of the [[Lebanese Basketball League]]. He has previously played for the [[Los Angeles Lakers]], [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], and [[Dallas Mavericks]] of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA), and is a former All-[[Big Ten Conference]] [[Guard (basketball)|guard]] who played three seasons for the [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan Wolverines]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/college/northwestern/chi-081026-michigan-basketball-big-ten,0,1668328.story |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081030073216/http://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/college/northwestern/chi-081026-michigan-basketball-big-ten%2C0%2C1668328.story |url-status=dead |archive-date=October 30, 2008 |title=Michigan preview |access-date=November 2, 2008 |date=October 26, 2008 |work=[[Chicago Tribune]] }}</ref>

He decided to forgo his final year of collegiate eligibility and declare himself [[Eligibility for the NBA Draft|eligible]] for the [[2010 NBA draft]], but went undrafted. He signed with the Cavaliers of the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). He began his second year injured and rehabbed for two months in the [[NBA Development League|NBA D-League]] with Cavaliers' affiliate, the [[Canton Charge]], before being re-signed by the Cavaliers. He signed with BC Azovmash of Ukraine in September 2012 and spent 2012–13 playing in the [[Ukrainian Basketball SuperLeague]]. For the following two seasons he split time in the NBA, NBA D-League and in the [[Turkish Basketball Super League]]. He is an NBA D-League All-star and six-time D-League performer of the week. He has set single-game scoring records for the Legends, Charge and D-Fenders franchises.

===Freshman year===
Prior to the 2007–08 basketball season, Freshman Harris was selected as a second team pre-season All-[[Big Ten Conference]] selection.<ref name=BTMP&AC/> He started every game for the [[2007–08 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mgoblue.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/111108aaa.html|title=Notes & Quotes: Michigan 77, Michigan Tech 55|access-date=March 15, 2015|date=November 11, 2008|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com}}</ref> He scored 13 points and tallied 4 steals in his debut on November 9 against {{cbb link|2007|sex=men|team=Radford Highlanders|school=Radford University|title=Radford}}.<ref>{{cite news|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=273130130|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150403002014/http://espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=273130130|url-status=dead|archive-date=April 3, 2015|title=Michigan 82, Radford 55|access-date=March 17, 2015|date=November 9, 2007|publisher=[[ESPN]]|agency=Associated Press}}</ref>  After the 2007–08 NCAA basketball season, Harris was selected as a second team All-Big Ten Conference selection and an All-Freshman team selection.  He led the Wolverines in scoring (16.4), assists (2.8), [[steal (basketball)|steals]] (1.5), minutes (32.9) and [[free throw]] percentage (82.0).<ref name=HRATSTaAFT>{{cite web|url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/031008aag.html|title=Indiana's White Named Big Ten Player of the Year by Coaches and Media: Purdue's Painter claims Coach of the Year accolades, Boilermakers' Kramer nabs Defensive Player of the Year honors, Hoosier Gordon earns Freshman of the Year laurels, and Wisconsin's Bohannon collects Sixth Man of the Year honor|access-date=June 12, 2011|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=MGoBlue.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120212082939/http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/031008aag.html|archive-date=February 12, 2012|url-status=dead|df=mdy-all}}</ref>  Among his highlights during the season were being named to the [[Great Alaska Shootout]] tournament team, becoming the fourth U-M freshman to score over 500 points in first season (516), and setting the U-M freshman record for [[free throw]]s made in a season while playing at least 20 minutes and starting every game.<ref name=MH*/>  During the season, he keyed the first three-game winning streak of the season for the team, which earned him his first Big Ten Player of the Week Award.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://bigten.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/021808aaa.html|title=Michigan Freshman Named Player of the Week: Harris averages 21 points in two triumphs|access-date=April 18, 2009|date=February 18, 2008|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|website=CSTV.com|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090108233444/http://bigten.cstv.com/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/021808aaa.html|archive-date=January 8, 2009|url-status=dead}}</ref>

=== Return to Cleveland (2012) ===
On February 21, the Cleveland Cavaliers announced they had signed Harris to a 10-day contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cleveland.com/cavs/index.ssf/2012/02/cleveland_cavaliers_sign_manny.html|title=Cleveland Cavaliers sign Manny Harris to a 10-day deal|access-date=February 21, 2012|date=February 21, 2012|publisher=[[The Plain Dealer|Cleveland.com]]}}</ref> He was re-signed on March 2 to a second 10-day contract.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ohio.com/news/break-news/cavs-re-sign-manny-harris-to-second-10-day-contract-1.268127|title=Cavs re-sign Manny Harris to second 10-day contract |access-date=March 3, 2012|date=March 2, 2012|work=[[Akron Beacon Journal]]|author=Lloyd, Jason}}</ref> After the second 10-day contract expired on March 11 and with the trade deadline approaching on March 15, the Cavaliers opted not to sign Harris to a guaranteed contract for the rest of the season.

==Personal life==
His name, Corperryale, is a combination of the names of his [[cousin]] (Corrine), an uncle (Perry) and the "ale" of his immediate siblings—Janelle, Jerrelle and Al.  He has a total of nine brothers and sisters and is the son of Merrick (Harris-Carter) and James Carter.<ref name=MH*/> Harris' middle name, Lādorable, is derived from his mother's reaction that he was "adorable" when she first saw him.<ref name=oram>{{cite web |last1=Oram |first1=Bill |title=More to Lakers' Harris than a name? |url=https://www.ocregister.com/2014/02/02/more-to-lakers-harris-than-a-name/ |website=The Orange County Register |access-date=September 15, 2024 |date=February 2, 2014}}</ref> The source of his nickname, "Manny", is given differing accounts by his parents: his mother claims that it was because he "looked like a grown man" as a baby while his father claims it was after the character [[Manny Ribera]] in ''[[Scarface (1983 film)|Scarface]]''.<ref name=oram /> During the 2013–14 season, the @DFenders and @nbadleague Twitter accounts occasionally referred to Harris using the hashtag #MichiganMamba.<ref name=NBADLscoringlead/><ref>{{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/DFenders/status/421859330309124097|title=@DFenders status update|access-date=January 11, 2014|date=January 10, 2014|publisher=[[Twitter]]|author=Los Angeles D-Fenders|author-link=Los Angeles D-Fenders}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/DFenders/status/418968080077697024|title=@DFenders status update|access-date=January 11, 2014|date=January 2, 2014|publisher=[[Twitter]]|author=Los Angeles D-Fenders|author-link=Los Angeles D-Fenders}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/nbadleague/status/422926503031345152|title=@nbadleague status update|access-date=January 14, 2014|date=January 13, 2014|publisher=[[Twitter]]|author=NBA Development League|author-link=NBA Development League}}</ref> Upon being called up to the NBA, @LakerNation used the nickname once.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://twitter.com/LakerNation/status/423869347434475520|title=@LakerNation status update|access-date=January 17, 2014|date=January 16, 2014|publisher=[[Twitter]]|author=Laker Nation}}</ref>
